HARD-001: Remove Development Origins from Production Security Configuration
cards.description:
Production CORS and Better Auth trusted-origin configuration currently retains localhost/development origins.

**Required Changes**

- Remove localhost origins from production CORS allowlists.
- Remove localhost from production Better Auth trusted origins.
- Keep localhost available in development only.
- Confirm credentialed APIs only allow expected production origins.
- Verify unauthenticated public APIs still behave as intended.

items.name: Production only trusts approved production domains.
Credentialed cross-origin requests from unauthorized origins fail.
Vercel frontend can communicate with Render backend normally.

cards.title: HARD-002: Review Public Swagger Exposure
cards.description:
Swagger documentation is currently part of the unauthenticated attack surface identified by the audit.

‌

**Required Changes**

- Determine whether production Swagger is required.
- If not required:
  - Disable Swagger in production.
- If required:
  - Consider authentication/IP restrictions.
  - Ensure no sensitive internal information is exposed.
- Keep Swagger available for local development where useful.

items.name: Public Swagger is disabled or intentionally approved.
Development Swagger remains available if required.
Swagger does not expose secrets or internal credentials.

cards.title: SEC-003: Restore Login CSRF Protection
cards.description:
The custom email sign-in wrapper bypasses Better Auth’s request-based login CSRF protection because the incoming HTTP request is not passed through Better Auth’s normal HTTP middleware.

A malicious website could potentially submit the attacker’s own credentials to the Gaffer login endpoint and cause the victim’s browser to become authenticated as the attacker.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts
Better Auth sign-in integration
```

**Required Changes**

- Restore request-aware CSRF protection.
- Either:
  - Validate `Origin` / Fetch Metadata on the NestJS sign-in endpoint, or
  - Route sign-in through Better Auth’s HTTP handler.
- Reject inappropriate cross-origin form submissions.
- Preserve normal same-origin JSON authentication.
- Do not break Google/OAuth login flows.

items.name: Cross-site form login cannot create a session.
Appropriate Origin/Fetch Metadata validation is covered by tests.

cards.title: SEC-008: Rate Limit and Cache Public Dashboard Queries
cards.description:
Public dashboard endpoints can perform relatively expensive database work without application-level throttling or response caching.

Player requests can return up to 500 rows while also calculating per-player match statistics.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/public-api/public-dashboard.controller.ts
backend/src/public-api/public-dashboard.service.ts
backend/src/public-api/public-api.schemas.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Add rate limiting for anonymous/public dashboard endpoints.
- Cache suitable public responses.
- Review the maximum `500` player result limit.
- Benchmark worst-case queries.
- Inspect database query plans.
- Ensure filters remain bounded.
- Prevent repeated identical anonymous requests from repeatedly performing expensive aggregation.

items.name: Frequently requested public data can be served from cache.
Queries remain performant as dataset size increases.
Rate limiting does not interfere with normal browsing.

cards.title: SEC-002: Add Distributed Rate Limiting to Authentication Endpoints
cards.description:
The custom NestJS authentication wrappers call Better Auth APIs directly. This bypasses Better Auth’s HTTP router rate limiter.

Affected flows include:

- Sign in
- Sign up
- Verification email resend

This could allow credential stuffing, email bombing, and excessive backend/email-provider resource usage.

The audit recommends a shared production-safe rate limiter with limits that work across backend instances.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts
backend/src/auth/auth.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Add application-level rate limiting to public authentication routes.
- Rate limit:
  - `/auth/sign-in`
  - Sign-up route
  - Verification email resend route
- Use separate policies for:
  - Password attempts
  - Email-sending operations
- Rate limiting must work across multiple Render/backend instances.
- Do not rely exclusively on in-memory counters.
- Preserve generic/uniform authentication error messages.
- Avoid exposing whether an email/account exists.

**Security Verification**

```
Exceed sign-in limit
→ Expect 429

Exceed email-send limit
→ Expect 429

Repeat requests across multiple backend instances
→ Limit must still apply
```

items.name: Repeated authentication attempts eventually return 429 Too Many Requests.
Concurrent requests cannot trivially bypass the limit.
A second application instance shares rate-limit state.
Error messages do not introduce account enumeration.

cards.title: SEC-011: Update Vulnerable Dependency Chains
cards.description:
The audit found dependency advisories in both frontend and backend dependency trees.

**Required Changes**

- Run fresh dependency audits.
- Inspect dependency trees.
- Update affected package chains where safe.
- Avoid blindly running breaking upgrades.
- Reassess whether affected functionality is reachable.
- Move CLI-only tooling out of production dependencies where possible.
- Specifically review whether `shadcn` needs to exist in production dependencies.

**Commands / Checks**

```
npm audit --omit=dev
npm ls
```

Run separately for:

```
/backend
/frontend
/root
```

cards.title: SEC-005: Prevent CSV Formula Injection
cards.description:
CSV output escapes normal CSV characters but does not protect against spreadsheet formulas.

A user-controlled value beginning with characters such as:

```
=
+
- 
@
```

could be interpreted as a spreadsheet formula when an exported report is opened.

**Affected Code**

```
frontend/src/features/statistics/team-report-model.ts
frontend/src/features/statistics/report-export.ts
backend/src/statistics/statistics.service.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Harden `csvCell`.
- Neutralize cells beginning with spreadsheet formula characters.
- Account for leading:
  - Whitespace
  - Tabs
  - Control characters
- Continue performing normal CSV escaping for:
  - Quotes
  - Commas
  - Newlines
- Apply protection to all user-controlled report values including:
  - Team names
  - Competition names
  - Opponent names
  - Player names

items.name: Values beginning with = appear as literal text.
Values beginning with + appear as literal text.
Values beginning with - appear as literal text.
Values beginning with @ appear as literal text.
Leading whitespace/control characters cannot bypass protection.

cards.title: SEC-004: Minimize Player Roster API Response
cards.description:
`GET /player/team` returns significantly more athlete information than the player roster UI requires.

The current response can expose teammate fields including:

- Exact date of birth
- Internal user ID
- Status
- Internal timestamps

The team authorization boundary is working, but the response contains unnecessary personal information.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/player/player.service.ts
backend/src/athletes/athletes.service.ts
backend/src/database/schema/index.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Create an explicit player-facing roster DTO.
- Return only fields required by the roster UI.
- Remove:
  - Exact `dateOfBirth`
  - Internal `userId`
  - Internal timestamps
  - Other unnecessary internal fields
- If age is required, calculate/derive it server-side rather than exposing DOB.
- Do not return raw database athlete objects directly.

items.name: Exact date of birth is absent.
Internal timestamps are absent unless explicitly necessary.
Tests verify the exact response contract.

cards.title: SEC-001: Restrict Team Updates to Coaches
cards.description:
Assistants are currently able to modify the team name and colour through the coach-level `PATCH /teams` endpoint.

The endpoint validates that the user has a session but does not enforce coach-level membership before calling the team update service. The underlying lookup accepts both coaches and assistants.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/teams/teams.controller.ts
backend/src/teams/teams.service.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Require coach membership before allowing `PATCH /teams`.
- Do not rely only on the controller for authorization.
- Enforce the coach requirement inside the service or a shared authorization guard.
- Ensure assistants cannot modify:
  - Team name
  - Team colour
  - Other coach-only team identity/settings
- Ensure competition-team display names cannot indirectly be changed by an assistant.

**Security Verification**

```
Sign in as assistant
→ PATCH /teams
→ Expect 403
→ Verify database unchanged

Sign in as coach
→ PATCH /teams
→ Expect successful update
```

items.name: Coach can update the team successfully.
Assistant request causes no database changes.
Competition-team display names remain unchanged after an unauthorized request.
Add/update automated tests covering coach and assistant roles.

cards.title: SEC-006: Fix Failed Logout Session Handling
cards.description:
The frontend currently clears its local authentication state even when `/auth/sign-out` fails.

Because the actual session cookie is `HttpOnly`, JavaScript cannot remove it. A failed backend logout can therefore leave the server session active even though the UI appears logged out. Reloading the page may restore the session.

**Affected Code**

```
frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx
backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Do not present logout as successfully completed when server revocation fails.
- Detect server logout failure.
- Inform the user appropriately.
- Retry logout when connectivity becomes available.
- Ensure UI state accurately represents server session state.
- Provide safe handling for offline logout attempts.

items.name: UI does not falsely claim that the secure session has ended.
Reload after failed logout produces expected authenticated state.
Retry flow successfully revokes session when connectivity returns.

cards.title: SEC-007: Prevent Verification and Invite Tokens from Being Logged in Production
cards.description:
When `BREVO_API_KEY` is missing, the email implementation logs complete verification/invitation URLs.

This development fallback is not currently restricted to development environments. If production email configuration breaks, bearer URLs could enter centralized production logs.

**Affected Code**

```
backend/src/email/email.ts
```

**Required Changes**

- Fail closed in production if required email configuration is missing.
- Never log complete:
  - Verification URLs
  - Invite URLs
  - Player claim URLs
  - Bearer tokens
- Allow link logging only in an explicitly development environment.
- Redact tokens from production logs.
- Do not return success when production email delivery was not actually configured.

items.name: Production startup/use without required email configuration does not expose links.
Complete bearer URLs never appear in production logs
Development environment can retain an intentional developer fallback.
Failed production email delivery is not reported as success.
Logs contain no reusable verification/invite credentials.

cards.title: SEC-009: Add Browser Security Headers
cards.description:
The repository does not currently define several browser security headers.

The audit specifically mentions:

- Content Security Policy
- Frame protection / `frame-ancestors`
- `X-Content-Type-Options`
- `Referrer-Policy`

The live Vercel/Render responses were not tested, so existing platform-level headers should be inspected before implementing changes.

**Affected Areas**

```
backend/src/main.ts
frontend/vercel.json
Vercel configuration
Render configuration
```

**Required Changes**

- Inspect existing production response headers.
- Add a tested CSP.
- Add `frame-ancestors` protection.
- Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Configure an appropriate `Referrer-Policy`.
- Consider HSTS only after confirming hosts are HTTPS-only.
- Avoid breaking third-party integrations.

**Regression Testing**
Test:

- Google OAuth
- PWA functionality
- Maps
- CSV exports
- PDF exports
- API requests
- Better Auth
- External services used by Gaffer

items.name: Production responses contain agreed security headers.
No required assets are blocked by CSP.

cards.title: SEC-010: Disable PowerSync Temporary Development Tokens in Production
cards.description:
Both PowerSync configuration templates currently allow temporary development tokens:

```
allow_temporary_tokens: true
```

The audit could not confirm which configuration is currently deployed. Gaffer Security Audit

**Affected Code**

```
powersync/service.yaml
powersync-recovery/service.yaml
```

**Required Changes**

- Inspect live PowerSync configuration.
- Disable temporary development tokens in production.
- Restrict PowerSync dashboard permissions.
- Confirm only authorized operators can access token-management functionality.
- Keep development conveniences isolated from production.

items.name: Production has temporary development tokens disabled.

cards.title: S2: API for Team Formation and Tactics
cards.description:
Implement and document a **public, read-only API** for Gaffer’s football formations and tactical approaches.

The API must allow external users/applications to retrieve supported formation and tactic reference data without authentication, while ensuring that **no team, player, coach, account, email or session data is exposed**.

The implementation includes the `/v1/formations` and `/v1/tactics` endpoints, optional filtering by ID, consistent JSON response structures, error handling, CORS configuration for the public routes, and interactive Swagger API documentation.

The API should be accessible through both the Gaffer frontend proxy and the deployed backend and must remain `GET`-only.

cards.title: S1-09 User Profile Management
cards.description:
**User Story:**
**As a logged-in user, I want to view and edit my profile so that I can keep my personal/account information up to date.**


Implement a profile page where the authenticated user can view their existing profile information and update the fields that are allowed to be edited.

items.name: Logged-in user can access their Profile page
Existing information is pre-filled when editing
User can edit permitted profile fields
User receives success feedback after updating
User cannot edit another user's profile
Profile page matches existing application styling

cards.title: S1-10 Features Page
cards.description:
**User Story:**
**As a user, I want to view the features offered by the Sport Coaching Tool so that I can understand what the application can help me do.**


Create a user-facing Features page that presents and explains the main capabilities available within the Sport Coaching Tool.

items.name: User can access the Features page
Each feature has a clear description
Appropriate icons/visual elements are included where useful
Navigation to/from the Features page works correctly
